Report DescriptionCALLER STATED THE NAVY HAS RADIATION STAGING YARDS ON PARCEL C ACROSS THE STREET FROM FOOD TRUCKS AND WHERE PEOPLE ARE LIVING. THIS HAS BEEN ONGOING ON SINCE 12MARCH2024. CALLER STATED THE NAVY REPORTED THE DETECTION OF PLUTONIUM 249 ON PARCEL C ON NOV 2024. THE NAVY HAS SINCE TAKEN THE AIR MONITORING DATA INFORMATION FROM 2024 OFF THEIR SITE. (PREVIOUS NRC REPORT # 1342958)

SkyTruth Analysis

Reported Spill Volume: 206 pound
Report Description///THIS IS AN UPDATE TO NRC REPORT 1476736/// THE MATERIAL HAS BEEN UPDATED FROM CHLORINE TO HCL GAS. THE AMOUNT OF MATERIAL OF MATERIAL THAT RELEASED WAS 206 POUNDS, WHICH THE CALLER STATED IS LESS THAN THE RQ. ORIGINAL: THE CALLER REPORTS THAT WHILE RUNNING A PROCESS, THE FACILITY DISCOVERED THAT NOT ALL DMTD HAD NOT DISSOLVED INTO THE PRODUCT. ALL THE CHLORINE WAS FED TO THE PRODUCT AND IN AN EFFORT TO REMOVE ALL MATERIAL, THE OIL PRODUCT WAS DECANTED TO A REACTOR THAT WAS NOT CONNECTED TO THE SCRUBBER. RESIDUAL CHLORINE CONTINUED TO VENT WHILE IT WAS IN THE SCRUB VESSEL. MATERIAL WAS TRANSFERRED BACK TO THE REACTOR, CONNECTED TO THE SCRUBBER, ONCE THE CHLORINE GAS WAS IDENTIFIED. 10 POUNDS OF CHLORINE WAS RELEASED.

properties.title: NRC Report: Jet Fuel: Jp-8 near Sheppard Air Force Base, TX
properties.summary: Incident Type: AIRCRAFT - NRC Report ID: 905706 - Medium Affected: SOIL - Suspected Responsible Party: SHEPPARD AIR FORCE BASE
properties.content:
NRC Report ID: 905706
Incident Time: 2009-05-14 19:00:00
Nearest City: Sheppard Air Force Base, TX
Incident Type: AIRCRAFT
Material: JET FUEL: JP-8
Medium Affected: SOIL
Suspected Responsible Party: SHEPPARD AIR FORCE BASE
Skytruth Analysis
Reported Spill Volume: 300 gallons
CALLER IS REPORTING THAT A TRAINING MISSION WAS BEING CONDUCTED USING A T-38C AIRCRAFT. THE AIRCRAFT LEFT THE RUNWAY AND TRAVELED APPROXIMATELY 50 FEET WHEN THE LANDING GEAR BROKE CAUSING THE AIRCRAFT TO COLLAPSE. THE COLLAPSE RESULTED IN A BROKEN LEFT WING AND A RUPTURED LOWER FUEL BLADDER. THE RUPTURE IN THE FUEL BLADDER RESULTED IN A RELEASE OF APPROXIMATELY 300 GALLONS OF JP 8 (A) FUEL ONTO THE SOIL. THE RELEASE IS CONTAINED ENTIRELY ON THE BASE AND HAS AFFECTED APPROXIMATELY 400 SQUARE FEET OF SOIL. CLEAN UP OPERATIONS WILL BEGIN ONCE THE AIRCRAFT CAN BE MOVED. THE AIRCRAFT WILL BE MOVED PENDING A MEETING OF THE INVESTIGATION BOARD. THE RUNWAY USED IS A SHARED RUNWAY WITH THE WICHITA FALLS AIRPORT AND IT WAS CLOSED BETWEEN 1400 ON 14-MAY AND 0530 ON 15-MAY. TWO INDIVIDUALS SUFFERED MINOR INJURIES AND WERE TRANSPORTED TO THE HOSPITAL.

Report Description/// CRITICAL INCIDENT COMMUNICATIONS (CIC) REPORT - INITIAL/FINAL - TUG AND BARGE FIRE - 22 APR 2025 /// INITIAL/FINAL INCIDENT TYPE: TUG AND BARGE FIRE LOCATION: VICTORIA BARGE CANAL, TEXAS TIME INCIDENT OCCURRED: 1750CST / 2250Z TIME OF INITIAL REPORT TO NCC: 1934 EST / 2334Z AMPLIFYING INFORMATION: • AT 1750L / 2250Z, USCG SECTOR CORPUS CHRISTI RECEIVED A REPORT OF A TUG AND BARGE FIRE IN THE VICTORIA BARGE CANAL AND INITIATED A CRITICAL INCIDENT COMMUNICATIONS (CIC) CALL. • THE PUSH AHEAD TUG WAS TRANSPORTING TWO BARGES CONTAINING GRAVEL WHEN IT BECAME COMPLETELY ENGULFED IN FLAMES AT MILE MARKER 20. • PUSH AHEAD TUG HAS 7500 GALLONS OF FUEL ON BOARD. • ALL SIX PEOPLE ON BOARD SAFELY DISEMBARKED THE TUG AND EVACUATED THE AREA VIA LIFE RAFT. • BEFORE THEIR DEPARTURE, THE TUG’S CREW UTILIZED THE VESSEL’S BOW THRUSTERS TO POSITION IT UP AGAINST THE SIDE OF THE CANAL. • CALHOUN COUNTY FIRE DEPARTMENT IS WORKING WITH THE LOCAL FACILITIES TO DETERMINE THE BEST METHOD TO EXTINGUISH THE VESSEL FIRE. • USCG WATERWAYS PREVENTION AND SMC HAVE BEEN NOTIFIED. • MOVEMENT WITHIN THE VICTORIA BARGE CANAL HAS BEEN RESTRICTED TO TUG MOVEMENT ONLY TO HELP FACILITATE RESPONSE EFFORTS. • THERE IS NO THREAT TO THE PUBLIC AND NO MEDIA INTEREST. • THE CIC PROCESS WAS STOOD DOWN WITH CONCURRENCE FROM BOTH AREAS.

UPDATE THE BLUE PRODUCT OBSERVED IN MUD CREEK HAS BEEN TRACED TO AN OFF PROPERTY SOURCE. HEPACO - CONTRACTOR HAS COLLECTED APPROXIMATELY 3,000 GALLONS FROM THE OUTFALL AT MUD CREEK AND AN UPSTREAM MANHOLE. THE SUBSTANCE WAS FOUND IN AN ADJACENT OUTFALL NEAR THE VORTEX AND IS BELIEVED TO HAVE ENTERED FROM AN OFF-PROPERTY STORMWATER PIPE. NO INJURIES OR EXPOSURES WERE REPORTED. A SMALL MUD CREEK WATERWAY WAS IMPACTED; HOWEVER, THE MATERIAL REMAINED CONTAINED WITHIN THE OUTFALL WITH NO DOWNSTREAM IMPACT.

Material: P-XYLENE
Medium Affected: AIR
Suspected Responsible Party: BP CHEMICAL CO.
Skytruth Analysis
DUE TO AN OPERATIONAL/PERMIT REVIEW, BP DETERMINED THAT EMISSIONS FROM ON-GOING BARGE LOADING OPERATIONS WERE NOT SUBJECT TO A FEDERALLY ENFORCEABLE PERMIT EVEN THOUGH THESE EMMISIONS HAD BEE COMMUNIED WITH THE ALABAMA DEPT OF ENVIRONMENTAL MANAGEMENT (ADEM). THE SITE LOADS BARGES WITH PARA-XYLENE AND HEAVY AROMATICS. PARA-XYLENE IS A HAP SUBJECT TO HON REGULATIONS. FOR THE GIVEN OPERATION, NO POLLUTION CONTROLS ARE REQUIRED BY THE REGULATION. WHILE THIS PROCESS HAS BEEN ONGOING FOR A FEW YEARS, DUE TO THE SITE'S REVIEW AND POSING THE SET OF CIRCUMSTANCES TO ADEM, THE SITE HAS COME TO THE CONCLUSION TODAY THAT THIS QUALIFIES AS A CERCLA CONTINUOUS RELEASE AND THIS REPORT IS TO SERVE AS THE INITIAL REPORT.

AT APPROXIMATELY 5:30 PM ON 10/26/12, PG&E EMPLOYEES WORKING ON LINE 132 WERE TURNING A VALVE WHEN THE VALVE CRACKED. THE VALVE IS 2 INCHES IN DIAMETER, AND WAS OPERATING AT 280 PSIG BEFORE THE CRACK. SERVICE TO 3 CUSTOMERS WAS AFFECTED. PG&E EMPLOYEES ON THE SCENE LET THE GAS FLOW OUT BECAUSE CLEARANCE WORK WAS BEING PERFORMED ON LINE 109; ONCE THAT WORK WAS FINISHED, LINE 109 COULD SUPPLY GAS TO THE CUSTOMERS AFFECTED BY THE OUTAGE ON LINE 132. FIRE DEPARTMENT AND SHERIFF'S DEPARTMENT PERSONNEL WERE ON-SCENE, BLOCKING OFF TRAFFIC AND PEDESTRIAN ACCESS TO THE AREA. properties.title: NRC Report: Unknown Material near Connellsville, PA
properties.summary: Incident Type: FIXED - NRC Report ID: 971678 - Medium Affected: AIR - Suspected Responsible Party: NATURAL GAS INDUSTRY
properties.content:
NRC Report ID: 971678
Incident Time: 2011-03-31 17:30:00
Nearest City: Connellsville, PA
Incident Type: FIXED
Material: UNKNOWN MATERIAL
Medium Affected: AIR
Suspected Responsible Party: NATURAL GAS INDUSTRY
Skytruth Analysis
MARCH 31, 2011 AT APPROX 12:00 A LIGHT MALODOROUS SMELL WAS NOTICED IN THE AIR. WHEN GETTING OUT OF A VEHICLE THAT SAME REPUGNANT SMELL WAS IN THE AIR ONLY IN A HIGHER CONCENTRATION AT THE INCIDENT LOCATION. THE REPORTING PARTY'S CHEST BEGAN TO BURN INTERNALLY AS IF THEY HAD HEARTBURN, THEY GOT AN INSTANT HEADACHE AND THEIR STOMACH BECAME UPSET. THEIR LIPS BECAME BITTER AND THE SMELL WAS ON THEIR CLOTHING. THEY CONTACTED NEIGHBORS WHO LIVE APPROX 1.5 MILE SOUTH OF INCIDENT LOCATION. THEY COULD SMELL THE HORRIBLE ODOR TOO AND WERE HAVING SYMPTOMS SIMILAR TO THE REPORTING PARTY. COLUMBIA GAS OF PA WAS CONTACTED TO REPORT THE SMELL BY THE REPORTING PARTY AND THEIR NEIGHBORS. A FIELD TECH ARRIVED AT THE NEIGHBORS HOME SHORTLY AFTER THE PHONE CALL. THE TECH INFORMED THE REPORTING PARTY THAT IT WAS NOT FROM COLUMBIA GAS BUT COULD BE COMING FROM A WELL SITE NEARBY. A FOLLOW UP CALL FROM THE REPORTING PARTY'S OFFICE AND THEY SPOKE WITH A CUSTOMER SERVICE REP. THEY DID NOT HAVE ANY DOCUMENTATION OF THE CALL PLACED TO THEIR EMERGENCY LINE. THEY WERE ASKED TO PLEASE RESEARCH AND GET BACK WITH THE REPORTING PARTY. CUSTOMER SERVICE REP TOLD THEM THAT THE HORRIBLE SMELLS ARE NOT FROM COLUMBIA GAS LINES BUT ARE FROM THE DEEP MARCELLUS WELLS THEMSELVES AND THAT THESE WELLS ARE RELEASING GASES IN THE NIGHT. THEY ARE RECEIVING SEVERAL PHONE CALLS CONCERNING THE ODORS. PLEASE INVESTIGATE THIS SITUATION AS THIS ODOR HAS BEEN PRESENT BEFORE ON DECEMBER 10, 2010 AND DECEMBER 11, 2010. BOTH DAYS 911 WAS CONTACTED AND ON BOTH DAYS THE REPORTING PARTY WAS ILL FROM SMELLING THIS ODOR.
